coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: P10
names: P10 -- landscaped center island, Mission Bay Circle roundabout
record.summary: The landscaped center island (grass, trees) of the 'Mission Bay Circle' roundabout in Mission Bay, where Mission Bay Drive, Owens, Channel and Mission Bay Boulevard meet; a real, already-built park feature distinct from the surrounding road pavement, per satellite imagery and this project's owner-guided tracing. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P10' among the parcels already managed by SF Recreation and Parks (not among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), consistent with it being complete by that date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- owner-guided satellite trace, not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team. street_clip_exempt=true: this is a real roundabout center island, inherently ringed by the circulating roadway in DataSF's curb data -- clipping it against the generic street buffer would cut real, visible parts of the island, not a mispositioning artifact.
notes.digitized_from: Hand-traced from satellite imagery (contextily/Esri World Imagery), guided directly by the owner's own marked-up screenshot (their drawn outline extracted from the photo via ORB feature-matching/homography rather than re-estimated by eye) -- same technique used for P11/P11A.

milestones.text: Already part of RPD's managed open-space inventory (not listed among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), per OCII's Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation to the Mission Bay CAC -- an upper bound on when this island was built, not its actual construction date

open_questions: No public source (SF Rec & Park, OCII, SFMTA, news) names this island or gives its own landscaping/construction date; the Sept 2023 OCII document only establishes that it existed and was already managed by that date, which is an upper bound, not a build date. It is presumed built alongside the Mission Bay Circle roundabout itself, whose own original construction date was not independently confirmed either (a 2021 Streetsblog SF article describes a later proposal for an added bike ring around the roundabout, not its original construction).
Owner/operator beyond 'part of RPD's Mission Bay open-space inventory' not confirmed by any source found.

record.notes: Center island of the real 'Mission Bay Circle' roundabout at the south end of the Mission Bay Circle/Owens St area, matching plan label P10. Landscaped with grass and trees; the roundabout's own median (P11A) and connector strip (P11) are tracked separately.
